title: Cleaning and sampling protocol for analysis of mercury and dissolved organic matter in freshwater systems
author: Bravo, Kothawala, et al.
materials: Here, we provide a complete list of materials needed to achieve effective sampling of the typically low ambient Hg levels found in freshwaters. To prevent contamination, we describe a protocol for equipment cleaning and sample processing. As there is no consensus on reporting IHg and MeHg concentration from filtered or unfiltered water fractions, we give details for collecting both water fractions: filtered (dissolved) and unfiltered (total). Although detailed protocols for collection of water with low Hg levels are available (e.g. https://water.usgs.gov/owq/FieldManual/chapter5/pdf/5.6.4.B_v1.0.pdf), here we describe an updated, simple and didactic protocol for collecting samples from freshwater ecosystems for Hg analyses. Furthermore, as Hg binds strongly to organic matter, we include a procedure to collect samples for determining dissolved and total organic carbon concentration (DOC and TOC) as well as DOM composition. Consequently, this protocol can be extremely helpful for non-experts in Hg sampling and analysis, as well as for all Hg research focusing on the role of organic matter composition related to Hg concentrations in the water [[5], [6], [7], [8], [9]]. It is noteworthy to mention that this protocol does not provide guidelines on the sampling design. The users of this protocol are encouraged to plan their sampling considering the optimal site location (e.g. deepest point of lake, distance from shoreline, etc.), depth (e.g. hypolimnion, epilimnion, etc), number of replicates, number of times the sampling will be performed in a year, etc. It is also important to highlight that because the choice of material used to sample with is glass (instead of PTFE), this protocol is not suitable for seawaters and water with ultra trace Hg levels (i.e. below 0.01 ng L−1 for IHg and 0.002 ng L−1 for MeHg).

Different methods can be used to measure IHg and MeHg [10]. IHg and MeHg concentrations were measured using species-specific isotope dilution and capillary gas chromatography (Trace GC Ultra, Thermo Fisher, Waltham, MA, USA equipped with a TriPlus RSH auto-sampler) hyphenated to a inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometer (Thermo X Series 2) [11,12]. The detection limits of this method are 0.02 ng L−1 for IHg and 0.005 ng L−1 for MeHg. Total-Hg concentration was calculated by adding IHg and MeHg concentrations. The measurement error (calculated by analyzing each sample three times) was less than 2.6% and 3.8% for IHg and MeHg concentrations, respectively [9] (Fig. 6).Fig. 6Mass chromatograms of two samples with contrasting methylmercury and inorganic mercury concentrations and different blank (Blk) samples that tested: i) the reagents (Blk-Reagent); ii) the sampling, handling, storage and reagents (Blk-Unfiltered); and iii) the sampling, handling, filtering, storage and reagents (Blk-Filtered). The lines represent the average of 3 replicate samples (each of them calculated by three analytical replicates).Fig. 6

steps.title: Prepare sample bottles
steps.instruction: Gather four types of containers: (1) 250 mL amber borosilicate glass bottle for unfiltered total‑Hg, IHg and MeHg; (2) 250 mL amber borosilicate glass bottle for filtered total‑Hg, IHg and MeHg; (3) 60 mL glass vial for unfiltered TOC; (4) 60 mL glass vial for filtered DOC, fluorescence, anions and cations.

steps.title: Wear gloves and label containers
steps.instruction: Put on nitrile gloves and clearly label each bottle and vial with the sample name and the intended analysis (e.g., “Sample‑01 Mercury unfiltered”, “Sample‑01 TOC unfiltered”, etc.).

steps.title: Condition bottles for unfiltered samples
steps.instruction: Prepare the unfiltered containers by rinsing them with site water before sample collection.

substeps.instruction: Fill a bit more than half of the 250 mL amber glass bottle (Mercury unfiltered) with site water, immerse the bottle closed to avoid the surface microlayer, shake vigorously, then discard the water downstream. Repeat three times.
Fill the 60 mL glass vial (TOC unfiltered) with site water, shake vigorously, discard the water downstream, and repeat three times.

steps.title: Collect unfiltered Hg sample
steps.instruction: After conditioning, fill the 250 mL amber glass bottle (Mercury unfiltered) with site water leaving about 0.5 cm headspace, add 250 µL concentrated HCl (Ultrex II ultrapure reagent, J.T. Baker), close the screw cap, shake gently, keep the bottle cold and dark in the field cooling box, and store at 4 °C in the refrigerator (or ship immediately).

steps.title: Collect unfiltered TOC sample
steps.instruction: Fill the 60 mL glass vial (TOC unfiltered) completely, ensuring no bubbles or headspace, keep it cold and dark in the field, store at 4 °C in the refrigerator (or ship immediately), then acidify with 100 µL of 2 M HCl and preserve at 4 °C until analysis.

steps.title: Collect filtered DOC sample
steps.instruction: Filter site water through a Sterivex filter using a syringe and collect the filtered water in the 60 mL glass vial (DOC filtered).

substeps.instruction: Rinse the syringe three times with site water.
Connect the Sterivex filter to the syringe, start filtering, and discard the first 20 mL of water.
Rinse the 60 mL glass vial by filling it with the remaining ~30 mL, shaking vigorously, and discarding the water; repeat this rinse two more times (total three rinses).

After rinsing, filter site water and fill the vial completely (no bubbles, no headspace). Keep the vial cold and dark in the field, store at 4 °C in the refrigerator (or ship immediately). Acidify with 100 µL of 2 M HCl prior to analysis, then in the laboratory adjust to pH 3.5 and preserve at 4 °C. Preserve a subsample before acidification for fluorescence, anions and cations measurements.

steps.title: Collect filtered Hg sample
steps.instruction: Filter site water for total‑Hg, IHg and MeHg analyses using a Sterivex filter and collect the filtrate in amber glass bottles.

substeps.instruction: Using the syringe and Sterivex filter, filter 60 mL of water into the 250 mL amber glass bottle (Mercury filtered), shake vigorously, discard the filtrate, and repeat two more times (total three 60 mL filtrations).
Filter 250 mL of site water into the same amber glass bottle, avoiding the surface microlayer by immersing the syringe at least 10 cm below the water surface.
Add 250 µL concentrated HCl (33–36%, Ultrex II ultrapure reagent, J.T. Baker, Phillipsburg, NJ, USA) to the bottle, close, and shake gently.
Keep the bottle cold and dark in the field, store at 4 °C in the refrigerator (or ship immediately).

steps.title: Bag and transport samples
steps.instruction: Place each sample container individually into a zip‑sealed Minigrip® plastic bag, double‑bag them, keep the bags cold and dark in the field, store the bags in a refrigerator upon return to the lab, and re‑bag until processing. Transport all sampling equipment and supplies in a clean plastic container with packing foam to protect the bottles.
